stem:
Ekta has two $3$ cm by $2$ cm rectangles. She joins them along a shared $2$ cm edge and asks how the perimeter changes.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: Call the answer "joined arrangement" only, without measuring the new outside boundary.
Add the two separate perimeters in full, counting the touching $2$ cm edges as if they were still outside.
After the join, the touching $2$ cm edges are inside, so the new perimeter is $16$ cm (a $6$ cm by $2$ cm rectangle), not $20$ cm.
Say that the new $16$ cm perimeter is what creates the joining along the $2$ cm edge, instead of joining first and then reading the outside boundary.

teacher.key_rationale: Joined perimeter is the new outside boundary; shared edges drop out: two $3\times2$ rectangles joined on $2$ cm make a $6\times2$ rectangle of perimeter $16$ cm. Relabeling, keeping internal edges, or reversing perimeter and join all miss that hinge.
